cohorts.name: Early Primary
cohorts.cognitive_focus: Sensory recognition, reflex instinct, trusted adult communication

modules.storyline: Golu the Elephant learns to drop to his knees and hold table legs when the ground dances.
dos: Drop to hands and knees
Cover head and neck under sturdy desk
Hold on until shaking stops
donts: Do not run outside while shaking
Do not stand near glass windows

modules.storyline: Buzzer the Bee hears the fire siren and walks calmly to the green playground gate.
dos: Hear alarm -> stop and listen to teacher
Stop, Drop, and Roll if clothes catch flame
Walk in single line to playground
donts: Never go back for toys or bags
Never hide under blankets or beds

cohorts.name: Upper Primary
cohorts.cognitive_focus: Basic hazard identification, exit sign recognition, emergency go-bag preparation

modules.storyline: Coastal storm preparation in Odisha: Assembling family emergency essentials.
dos: Pack torch, batteries, drinking water, first-aid, ORS
Shelter in core interior room away from glass
Listen to official radio bulletins
donts: Do not go outside during calm eye of the storm
Do not shelter under tall trees or utility poles

modules.storyline: Understanding fire types without unsupervised operation.
dos: P - Pull pin
A - Aim at base
S - Squeeze lever
S - Sweep side to side
donts: Never use water on electrical panel fires
Never use water on cooking oil pans

cohorts.name: Middle School
cohorts.cognitive_focus: Procedural exit differentiation, compound hazard logic, floor plan reading

modules.core_rule: Damaged Staircase Avoidance & Secondary Exit Routing
dos: Inspect stairs for major structural cracks before descending
Use alternate fire stairwell if primary is damaged
Help younger peers descend calmly
donts: Never use passenger lifts after earthquake
Never run down stairs while shaking is active

dos: Alert teacher immediately
Close laboratory fire doors to contain fumes
Evacuate upwind of building

cohorts.name: Secondary School
cohorts.cognitive_focus: Stress decision-making, triage communication, multi-condition compound disasters

dos: Check door temperature with back of hand
Seal bottom gap with damp jackets/towels
Stay low (<50cm) where air is breathable
Signal responders clearly from exterior window
donts: Never open hot doors into smoke

dos: State exact location: Building, Floor, Room Number
State hazard type and active spread
State number of trapped/injured persons
Report blocked escape corridors
donts: Do not shout or scream into line
Do not hang up until dispatcher confirms

cohorts.name: College & Young Adults
cohorts.cognitive_focus: Incident Command System (ICS), crowd management, mass casualty triage, disaster rumor debunking

dos: Direct crowd into steady single-file descent
Verify all classrooms on assigned floor are clear
Perform digital QR roll call at safe assembly zone
Transmit trapped manifest directly to NDRF search units
donts: Never allow crowd bottlenecking at exit doors
Never permit re-entry into evacuated building

dos: Tag RED: Immediate life threat (airway/severe bleeding)
Tag YELLOW: Delayed (fractures, stable)
Tag GREEN: Minor walking wounded
Tag BLACK: Deceased / Non-viable
donts: Do not move spinal injury casualties unless in immediate fire danger
